Title: Missing CSRF Protection in Flaskr Tutorial Example Application
Analysis:
The Flaskr tutorial application inside the repository (`examples/tutorial/flaskr/blog.py`) allows users to manage blog posts through state-changing actions via the `/create`, `/<int:id>/update`, and `/<int:id>/delete` routes. Since Flask does not include CSRF protection out of the box, and no CSRF tokens or origin checks are validated on the backend/rendered in the forms, these endpoints are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). An external attacker can craft an exploit page containing a hidden form that targets one of these endpoints (e.g. `/<int:id>/delete` or `/<int:id>/update`) and auto-submits it. When an authenticated user visits the attacker's page, their browser automatically includes the session cookie, executing the action on their behalf.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
An attacker hosts a malicious HTML page with the following payload:
```html
<body onload="document.forms[0].submit()">
  <form action="http://localhost:5000/1/delete" method="POST">
    <input type="submit" value="Delete Post">
  </form>
</body>
```
When an authenticated user (who is the author of post ID 1) visits this page, a POST request is automatically sent to the `/1/delete` endpoint. Since the browser includes the session cookie, Flaskr will delete the post with ID `1` on behalf of the victim.
